text: Fall. I once was flesh with hands so sure. A woodsman strong with love so pure. But cursing axe and rusted fate turn me to tin to mourn and weight. Each drop of rain a threat to me. Each joint to lock no fluid free. I'd freeze mid thought mid reach mid cry and wonder if machines can sigh. They said I lacked a human

Heart. But pain still bloom in every part. Not blood, but longing filled my core. For love I lost and felt no more. Then came a girl with storm lit eyes. And strangers bearing dreams and ties. They wound my key. They heard my plea. They dared to say there's hope for  me. Through haunted woods and witches flame, I clanked along in search of name. Not just in man, but something hope. A beating truth, a living soul. At oz I

Known, but for a heart to write love down. And what I found or what was shown was that I'd never been alone. For every tear I could not shed, still shimmerred in the words I said. And though I'm made of bolts and steel, I learned to hope is still to feel
